purpose: completed answer-blind clean-room reviewer decisions for the systematic MAP fidelity audit
reviewMethod: Fresh answerless browser-effective worksheet; scoring, rationales, keyed manifests, prior answers, tests, prior audits, and prior rubric reviews were treated as non-evidence. Auto-scored responses and constructed-response expectations were committed before any keyed reconciliation or manual rubric exposure.
answerEncoding: option/options are 1-based positions in the blind worksheet; matches maps row keys to 1-based choice positions; value stores the independently determined raw response for graph, numeric, and constructed-response items.

g5s-cr-001.value: The evidence supports conservation of matter because the sealed bag has the same total mass, 100 g, before and after dissolving. The tablet's matter did not disappear when it became invisible; it remained in the sealed bag dispersed/dissolved in the water.

g5s-cr-002.value: The stronger push produced a greater change in the car's motion. The identical car pushed with 3 N traveled 118 cm, while the car pushed with 1 N traveled only 45 cm under the same conditions, so a stronger push can produce a greater change in motion.

g5s-cr-003.value: One path is carbon dioxide and water from the nonliving environment into grass, then grass into a rabbit that eats it, and then into a fox that eats the rabbit. Decomposers break down wastes and dead organisms and return matter to soil and air, where producers can use it again.

g5s-cr-004.value: Reject the claim that the added material came chiefly from soil. The plant gained 18 g of dry mass (6 g to 24 g), while the dry soil lost only 4 g (700 g to 696 g), so soil loss cannot account for most of the plant's gain. The plant also had access to water and air, which supply material used to build plant matter.

g5s-cr-005.value: Soil loss increases as the slope becomes steeper in this model. The nearly flat tray lost 11 g, the medium-slope tray lost 25 g, and the steep tray lost 44 g, so the data show progressively greater soil loss with greater slope.

g5s-cr-006.value: Repairing the leaks appears to reduce water use: average outdoor use fell from 920 L/day to 610 L/day, a decrease of 310 L/day. A stronger comparison would also measure or record a relevant condition such as rainfall/weather or irrigation duration on the before-and-after days so the periods can be shown to be comparable.
